name: The Eyrie Vineyards
summary: Pioneering Willamette Valley Pinot noir producer. Its five estate vineyards are in the Dundee Hills, while the winery itself is in McMinnville. Its 1975 Reserve Pinot noir placed in the top ten at the 1979 Wine Olympics in Paris.

name: Abacela
summary: Umpqua Valley estate near Roseburg founded by Earl and Hilda Jones, the first winery in the Pacific Northwest to grow and produce varietal Tempranillo commercially. Its vines were first planted in 1995 and its first vintage was 1998.

name: King Estate Winery
summary: Family-owned winery near Lorane, southwest of Eugene, founded in 1991 by Ed King Jr. and Ed King III. Its 1,033-acre estate is certified organic and, since 2016, Biodynamic.

name: Valley View Winery
summary: Applegate Valley winery founded in 1972 by Frank Wisnovsky's family, taking the name of the vineyard Peter Britt started at Jacksonville in the 1850s. Frank's sons Mark and Michael became its owners in 2005.

name: Troon Vineyard
summary: Applegate Valley vineyard and winery that grew from Dick Troon's 1972 plantings. Bryan and Denise White bought it in 2017 and converted it to Demeter-certified Biodynamic farming.

name: Henry Estate Winery
summary: Family winery at Umpqua opened by Scott Henry in 1978 on a vineyard he had planted in 1972; it released its first wines the following year.

sources.title: Oregon winemaker Scott Henry dies at age 86 (Capital Press)
Henry Estate Winery patriarch dies at age 86 (The News-Review)

name: Girardet Vineyards and Winery
summary: Umpqua Valley estate at Tenmile, near Roseburg, founded in 1971 by Philippe and Bonnie Girardet and now run by their son Marc. Known for Baco noir.

sources.title: Philippe Girardet, Founder of Girardet Vineyards and Winery, Passes Away at 96 (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Cayuse Vineyards
summary: Christophe Baron's estate at Milton-Freewater on the Oregon side of the Walla Walla Valley, farmed with biodynamic methods on cobblestone ground.

sources.title: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater AVA (Wikipedia)

name: Maison Joseph Drouhin
summary: Burgundy wine producer and négociant founded in 1880, with vineyards from Chablis to the Côte Chalonnaise. It built Domaine Drouhin Oregon in the Dundee Hills.

name: Domaine Drouhin Oregon
summary: Dundee Hills winery established by the Drouhin family of Burgundy in 1987. Its first vintage, 1988, was made from purchased grapes, and its gravity-flow winery was built in 1989.

sources.title: Profiles in Pinot Noir: Domaine Drouhin (Wine Spectator)

name: Panther Creek Cellars
summary: Winery founded by Ken Wright in McMinnville in 1986 and sold in 1994. Later owned by Ron and Linda Kaplan and the Chambers family, it was bought by Bacchus Capital Management in 2013.

sources.title: Ken Wright lecture announcement (Linfield University news)
Ken Wright and Panther Creek Cellars (Great Northwest Wine)
Panther Creek Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Ken Wright Cellars
summary: Carlton winery founded by Ken Wright with the 1994 vintage, known for single-vineyard Pinot noir from sites across the northern Willamette Valley.

sources.title: Ken Wright Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)
Ken Wright lecture announcement (Linfield University news)

name: Beaux Frères
summary: Ribbon Ridge winery started by Michael Etzel on a former pig farm with his brother-in-law Robert Parker, with vines planted from 1988 and a first commercial release from the 1991 vintage. Maisons & Domaines Henriot bought a controlling interest in 2017.

sources.title: The Birth and Building of Beaux Frères (Wine Spectator)

name: Bethel Heights Vineyard
summary: Family winery in the Eola-Amity Hills founded in 1977 by twin brothers Ted and Terry Casteel, their wives Pat Dudley and Marilyn Webb, and Barbara Dudley. The winery was built and the first estate wines made in 1984.

name: Cristom Vineyards
summary: Eola-Amity Hills winery founded in 1992 by Paul and Eileen Gerrie on the abandoned Pellier Winery site and named after their children Christine and Tom.
address: 6905 Spring Valley Rd NW Salem, OR 97304

name: Argyle Winery
summary: Dundee winery founded in 1987 by Rollin Soles and Brian Croser in a former nut-processing plant, with sparkling wine as its signature. Lion Nathan acquired it with Croser's Petaluma company, and it is now owned by Distinguished Vineyards & Wine Partners.

sources.title: Rollin Soles Relinquishes Winemaker Title at Argyle (Wine Spectator)

name: ROCO Winery
summary: Winery of Rollin Soles and Corby Stonebraker-Soles, named for the two of them. They planted Wits' End Vineyard in 2001, made a first vintage in 2003 and built the winery in 2009.

sources.title: Rollin Soles Relinquishes Winemaker Title at Argyle (Wine Spectator)

name: Chehalem
summary: Newberg winery founded by Harry Peterson-Nedry in 1990, growing out of his Ridgecrest Vineyards. Bill Stoller became a co-owner by 1993 and the sole owner in 2018.

sources.title: Bill Stoller, Oregon Vintner and Philanthropist, Dies at Age 74 (Wine Spectator)

name: Willamette Valley Vineyards
summary: Publicly traded winery in Turner founded in 1983 by Jim Bernau and Don Voorhies and funded in part by small shareholders. It merged with Tualatin Estate Vineyards in 1997.

sources.title: The Jim Bernau story (Oregon State University College of Business)

name: Penner-Ash Wine Cellars
summary: Winery started in 1998 by Lynn and Ron Penner-Ash while Lynn was still at Rex Hill; the estate winery was built in 2005. Jackson Family Wines bought it in 2016.

sources.title: Penner-Ash Winery Purchased By California's Jackson Family Wines (Willamette Week)

address: 15771 NE Ribbon Ridge Road Newberg, OR 97132

name: Rex Hill
summary: Newberg winery founded in 1982 by Paul Hart and Jan Jacobsen on the site of a former fruit and nut drying facility. The founders handed it to the families behind A to Z Wineworks when they retired.

name: Evening Land Vineyards
summary: Winery founded by Mark Tarlov in 2005 that took a long lease on Seven Springs Vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills in 2007, with Dominique Lafon consulting. Rajat Parr and Sashi Moorman became partners and took over operations in 2014.

sources.title: Evening Land Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Lingua Franca
summary: Eola-Amity Hills winery founded by Master Sommelier Larry Stone on a 66-acre vineyard beside Seven Springs, with Dominique Lafon consulting and Thomas Savre as winemaker. Its first vintage was 2015, and Constellation Brands bought it in 2022.

sources.title: Exclusive: Constellation Buys Oregon's Lingua Franca (Wine Spectator)

name: Bergström Wines
summary: Dundee winery established in fall 1999 by John and Karen Bergström and their son Josh, with estate vineyards in the Dundee Hills, Ribbon Ridge and Chehalem Mountains.

name: Domaine Serene
summary: Dundee Hills estate founded in 1989 by Ken and Grace Evenstad, with a first commercial vintage in 1990. Ken Wright was its first winemaker.

sources.title: Ken Evenstad, Co-Founder of Oregon's Domaine Serene Winery, Dies at 77 (Wine Spectator)

name: Maisons & Domaines Henriot
summary: French wine group built around the Champagne house Henriot. It bought a controlling interest in Beaux Frères in 2017.

sources.title: The Birth and Building of Beaux Frères (Wine Spectator)

name: Jackson Family Wines
summary: California-based wine company that bought Penner-Ash Wine Cellars in 2016, adding to Oregon holdings that include Gran Moraine and Zena Crown vineyards.

sources.title: Penner-Ash Winery Purchased By California's Jackson Family Wines (Willamette Week)

name: A to Z Wineworks
summary: Oregon wine company founded by Bill and Deb Hatcher, Cheryl Francis and Sam Tannahill, who took over Rex Hill when its founders retired. Ste. Michelle Wine Estates acquired A to Z and Rex Hill in 2022.

name: HillCrest Vineyard
summary: Winery west of Roseburg founded by Richard Sommer in 1961, described as Oregon's first post-Prohibition estate winery and the site of the state's first Pinot noir plantings. Sold in 2003 to Dyson and Susan DeMara.

name: Charles Coury Vineyards
summary: Vineyard, nursery and winery run by Charles and Shirley Coury near Forest Grove from 1965 until financial strain forced a sale in 1978. The property was renamed David Hill Vineyards & Winery after 1992.

sources.title: Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Erath Winery
summary: Dundee winery founded by Dick Erath, which made its first commercial wine in 1972 and traded as Knudsen Erath from 1975 to 1988. Bought by Ste. Michelle Wine Estates in 2006.

sources.title: Erath Winery Collection: historical note (Linfield / Oregon Wine History Archive)
Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)
Ste. Michelle buys Oregon winery (NBC News / AP)

name: Knudsen Erath Winery
summary: Partnership between grower Cal Knudsen and winemaker Dick Erath, established in 1975 and described as the first commercial winery in the Dundee Hills. The partners separated in 1988 and Erath continued under his own name.

sources.title: Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)
Knudsen family and Knudsen Vineyards feature (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Ponzi Vineyards
summary: Founded in 1970 by Dick and Nancy Ponzi on land bought southwest of Portland in 1969; first Pinot noir vintage in 1974. The Bollinger family acquired the winery in 2021.

sources.title: The Bollinger Family to Acquire Ponzi Vineyards (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Adelsheim Vineyard
summary: Founded by David and Ginny Adelsheim, who bought land near Newberg in 1971, planted in 1972 and released their first wines in 1978. Described as the first winery in the Chehalem Mountains; fully owned by Jack and Lynn Loacker since 2017.

name: Sokol Blosser Winery
summary: Founded by Bill Blosser and Susan Sokol Blosser in 1971 in what is now the Dundee Hills AVA, with a first vintage in 1977. Opened a tasting room in 1978 and is now led by the second generation.
address: 5000 NE Sokol Blosser Lane, Dayton, OR 97114

name: Amity Vineyards
summary: Founded by Myron Redford in 1974 on a vineyard above the town of Amity planted in 1971; first vintage 1976. Bought in 2014 by Ryan and Eric Harms of Union Wine Company.

name: Elk Cove Vineyards
summary: Family-owned winery founded in 1974 by Pat and Joe Campbell near Gaston, the first winery in what is now the Yamhill-Carlton appellation.

sources.title: Joe Campbell, Pioneering Willamette Valley Winemaker, Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)

name: Tualatin Vineyards
summary: Established in 1973 near Forest Grove by Bill Fuller and Bill Malkmus. Owned by Willamette Valley Vineyards since 1997 and now known as Tualatin Estate Vineyard.
address: 10850 NW Seavey Road Forest Grove, Oregon 97116

name: St. Innocent Winery
summary: Winery founded by Mark Vlossak in 1988, known for single-vineyard wines from sites including Freedom Hill, Temperance Hill, Shea and Momtazi. It operated at Zenith Vineyard from 2006 and moved in 2019 to its Enchanted Way Vineyard in the South Salem Hills.

name: Cameron Winery
summary: Dundee winery founded in 1984 by John Paul with partners including his wife Teri Wadsworth and Bill and Julia Wayne of Abbey Ridge Vineyard. Its estate vineyard, Clos Electrique, surrounds the winery.

name: Archery Summit
summary: Dundee Hills winery established in 1993 by Gary Andrus and Nancy Andrus, the founders of Pine Ridge Vineyards in Napa. Andrus sold it in 2001 and it is now owned by Crimson Wine Group.

sources.title: Archery Summit Winery (The Prince of Pinot)

address: 18599 NE Archery Summit Road, Dayton, OR 97114

name: Brick House Vineyards
summary: Doug Tunnell's 40-acre estate in the Ribbon Ridge AVA, certified organic since 1990 and Demeter-certified biodynamic since 2005. Pinot noir was planted in 1990 and the first vintage was 1993; all fruit is estate grown.

sources.title: Brick House Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Patricia Green Cellars
summary: Winery founded in 2000 by Patty Green and Jim Anderson, who bought the former Autumn Wind cellar and vineyard in what is now the Ribbon Ridge AVA. Anderson has run it as owner and winemaker since Green's death in 2017.

sources.title: In Memoriam: Patty Green (Oregon Wine Press)
Jim Anderson Interview (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Torii Mor Winery
summary: Dundee Hills winery founded in 1993 by Donald Olson, M.D., to showcase fruit from his Olson vineyard, planted in 1972. Patty Green was its first winemaker.

sources.title: Torii Mor Winery (The Prince of Pinot)
In Memoriam: Patty Green (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Lange Estate Winery and Vineyards
summary: Dundee Hills family winery established in 1987 by Don and Wendy Lange, who moved from Santa Barbara and planted thirty acres. Their son Jesse took over the winemaking in 2005.

sources.title: Lange Estate Winery and Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
Lange Estate Winery and Vineyards: address (www.langewinery.com)

address: 18380 NE Buena Vista Drive Dundee, OR 97115

name: Brooks Wine
summary: Eola-Amity Hills winery founded by Jimi Brooks in 1998. After his death in 2004 it passed to his son Pascal, then eight, with his sister Janie Brooks Heuck as managing director and Chris Williams as winemaker from 2005.

sources.title: Brooks Wine: The People of Brooks

name: Maysara Winery
summary: The Momtazi family's winery at Momtazi Vineyard near McMinnville, with a first vintage in 2001. Moe and Flora Momtazi own it and their daughter Tahmiene makes the wines.

sources.title: Moe and Hanna Momtazi interview photograph (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Yamhill Valley Vineyards
summary: Family-owned winery in the McMinnville AVA with a first vintage in 1983, owned by Denis Burger, Elaine McCall and David Hinrichs. Stephen Cary led its winemaking from 1991 to 2016.

sources.title: Yamhill Valley Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
Yamhill Valley Vineyards Collection (Oregon Wine History Archive)
In Memoriam: Stephen Cary (Oregon Wine Press)

name: WillaKenzie Estate
summary: Yamhill-Carlton estate founded by Bernard and Ronni Lacroute, who bought a cattle farm in 1991, began planting in 1992 and made their first wine in a gravity-flow winery in 1995. Jackson Family Wines bought it in 2016.

sources.title: Jackson Family Continues Oregon Pinot Noir Expansion, Buying WillaKenzie Estate (Wine Spectator)

name: Evesham Wood
summary: Eola-Amity Hills winery launched in 1986 by Russ Raney. Russ and Mary Raney sold it and its Le Puits Sec Vineyard to Erin and Jordan Nuccio of Haden Fig in August 2010.

sources.title: Erin Nuccio, Evesham Wood | Haden Fig (Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers)

name: Stoller Family Estate
summary: Bill Stoller's winery on his family's former turkey farm. The first Stoller vintage was made at Chehalem in 2001, Melissa Burr was hired as its first dedicated winemaker in 2003, and construction of its own winery began in 2005.

name: Soter Vineyards
summary: Founded in 1997 by Tony and Michelle Soter with the purchase of Beacon Hill Vineyard. Since 2001 it has been based at Mineral Springs Ranch in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA, which was certified biodynamic in 2016.

name: Foris Vineyards
summary: Illinois Valley winery near Cave Junction in the Rogue Valley AVA. Ted and Meri Gerber bought land there in 1971, sold grapes to other winemakers for about 15 years and launched the Foris label in 1986.

name: Reustle-Prayer Rock Vineyards
summary: Umpqua Valley estate near Roseburg started by Stephen and Gloria Reustle, who bought 200 acres in 2001 and launched the winery in 2004. In 2003 they planted what is described as the first Gruner Veltliner in the United States.

sources.title: 2017 Pacific Northwest Winery of the Year: Reustle Prayer Rock Vineyard (Umpqua Valley Wineries)
Reustle-Prayer Rock Vineyards Grüner Veltliner (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Shea Wine Cellars
summary: Winery created by Dick and Deirdre Shea in 1999 to make wine from their Shea Vineyard in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA. It takes roughly a fifth to a quarter of the vineyard's fruit; the rest is sold to other wineries.

sources.title: Shea Vineyard and TuShea (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Lemelson Vineyards
summary: Winery founded by Eric Lemelson, who planted his first two acres of Pinot noir and Pinot gris in 1995. It owns about 120 acres of vineyards, including Stermer Vineyard at the winery, Chestnut Hill and Meyer.

name: Westrey Wine Company
summary: Winery founded in 1993 by Amy Wesselman and David Autrey, its name a blend of their surnames. It began with purchased fruit and now also farms the 22-acre Oracle Vineyard in the Dundee Hills, next to Abbey Ridge.

sources.title: Westrey Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Carlton Winemakers Studio
summary: Shared winemaking facility in Carlton opened in 2002 by Eric Hamacher, Luisa Ponzi and Ned and Kirsten Lumpkin, after Oregon law changed to let several independent wineries share one facility. Early tenants included Hamacher Wines, Lazy River and Andrew Rich.

name: Maison Louis Jadot
summary: Burgundy wine house, launched in 1859. In 2013 it bought the Résonance Vineyard in Yamhill-Carlton, its first project outside France, and later added a Dundee Hills site.

name: Résonance
summary: Maison Louis Jadot's Oregon winery, built around the Résonance Vineyard it bought in 2013. Its custom-built winery was first used for the 2018 harvest and the tasting room opened in May 2019.

name: Nicolas-Jay
summary: North Willamette Valley Pinot noir and Chardonnay estate founded in 2012 by Burgundian winemaker Jean-Nicolas Méo and music entrepreneur Jay Boberg. It farms its own organic Bishop Creek Vineyard.

name: Domaine Méo-Camuzet
summary: Côte d'Or domaine owned and run by Jean-Nicolas Méo, co-founder of Oregon's Nicolas-Jay.

name: Gran Moraine
summary: Jackson Family Wines' Yamhill-Carlton label, based on the 200-acre Gran Moraine Vineyard the company acquired in May 2013. It is made at the former Soléna Estate winery near Yamhill, which Jackson also bought.
address: 17090 NE Woodland Loop Rd Yamhill, OR 97148

name: Seven Hills Winery
summary: Walla Walla Valley winery started in 1988 by Casey and Vicky McClellan. It was based in Milton-Freewater, Oregon, from late 1989 until it moved to downtown Walla Walla, Washington, in 2000; Crimson Wine Group bought it in January 2016.

sources.title: Crimson Wine Group Buys 66 Acres of Walla Walla Valley Vines (Wine Spectator)

name: The Four Graces
summary: Dundee winery founded in 2003 by Steven and Paula Marie Black and named for their four daughters, with estate vineyards in the Dundee Hills and Yamhill-Carlton. Foley Family Wines bought it in 2014.

sources.title: Foley Family Wines Buys Oregon's The Four Graces (Wine Spectator)

name: Foley Family Wines
summary: Bill Foley's wine company, an active buyer of wineries since 1996. The Four Graces, bought in 2014, was its first Oregon acquisition.

sources.title: Foley Family Wines Buys Oregon's The Four Graces (Wine Spectator)

name: Benton-Lane Winery
summary: Willamette Valley estate straddling Benton and Lane counties north of Eugene, on property Steve and Carol Girard bought in 1988. Huneeus Vintners bought the winery, brand and inventory in 2018 while the Girards kept the 142-acre vineyard.

sources.title: Napa Valley's Huneeus Vintners Buys Oregon's Benton-Lane Winery (Wine Spectator)

name: Huneeus Vintners
summary: Napa Valley wine company, owner of Quintessa and Flowers, led by Agustín Huneeus Jr. It bought Benton-Lane Winery in Oregon in 2018.

sources.title: Napa Valley's Huneeus Vintners Buys Oregon's Benton-Lane Winery (Wine Spectator)

name: The Family Coppola
summary: Francis Ford Coppola's wine company. It announced the purchase of Vista Hills Vineyard in the Dundee Hills in late 2018 and launched an Oregon estate label there, first called Domaine de Broglie and later Domaine Lumineux.

sources.title: Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

name: Domaine Lumineux
summary: Coppola family-owned Oregon Pinot noir label, introduced in March 2019 as Domaine de Broglie at the former Vista Hills Vineyard. After a 2021 fire destroyed the Dayton tasting room it moved to Newberg and took its current name in early 2024.

sources.title: Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

name: Silver Oak
summary: Napa Valley winery owned by the Duncan family, who also own the Twomey Pinot noir brand. In September 2017 the family bought Dick Erath's Prince Hill Vineyard in the Dundee Hills as a Pinot noir source for Twomey.

sources.title: Exclusive: Silver Oak Owners Buy Oregon Vineyard from Dick Erath (Wine Spectator)

name: Chapter 24 Vineyards
summary: Willamette Valley Pinot noir producer launched in 2012 by Mark Tarlov after he left Evening Land, with Burgundy vigneron Louis-Michel Liger-Belair as partner and consultant. In 2016 its owners bought the Witness Tree property in the Eola-Amity Hills.

sources.title: Chapter 24 Wines Purchases Witness Tree and Five Other Vineyards in Oregon's Willamette Valley (Wine Spectator)

name: Maison Bleue
summary: Winery founded by Jon and Amy Meuret in Washington in 2007 and later based in Walla Walla. Willamette Valley Vineyards bought the brand in January 2018 and set aside 15 acres of its land in The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater for a Maison Bleue estate vineyard.

sources.title: Oregon's Willamette Valley Vineyards Buys Maison Bleue in Walla Walla Valley (Wine Spectator)
Willamette Valley Vineyards buys Maison Bleue (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Hood River Vineyards
summary: The oldest winery in the Columbia Gorge, started in 1981 by Cliff and Eileen Blanchette and their son Thomas. Anne and Bernie Lerch bought it in 1992 and farm about 50 acres.

sources.title: In the sweet spot for growing fruit, Anne and Bernie Lerch enjoy staying small (Columbia Gorge News)

name: Phelps Creek Vineyards
summary: Pinot noir specialist in the Columbia Gorge AVA at Hood River, founded by Robert Morus, with 30 acres of Pinot noir and Chardonnay first planted in 1989. Burgundian Alexandrine Roy has made all its wines since the 2012 vintage.

name: Domaine Marc Roy
summary: Family domaine in Gevrey-Chambertin, Burgundy, where Alexandrine Roy is the fourth-generation winemaker.

name: Watermill Winery
summary: Milton-Freewater winery established in 2005 by the Brown family, third-generation apple growers, in a renovated 1944 pea processing plant. The Foreman and Kleinman families became partners in 2017.

name: Zerba Cellars
summary: Milton-Freewater winery founded in 2001 by Cecil and Marilyn Zerba after 20 years in the nursery business. Its estate vineyards include Dad's Vineyard, Cockburn Ranch and Winesap Road Vineyard in The Rocks District.

name: Del Rio Vineyards
summary: Rogue Valley estate at Gold Hill on the former Del Rio pear orchard, which Californians Lee and Margaret Traynham bought in 1997 and converted to wine grapes with Rob and Jolee Wallace. Long a grape supplier to other wineries, it began bottling under its own label in 2004 and is one of the largest vineyards in Southern Oregon.

sources.title: Vine with a View (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Quady North
summary: Applegate Valley winery of Herb and Meloney Quady, on 100 acres they bought in 2005. Its estate blocks, Mae's Vineyard (2005) and Eevee's Vineyard (2011), are named for their daughters.

sources.title: An Interview With Herb Quady, Southern Oregon's Godfather Of Grapes (Sprudge)
Herb Quady resigns from Troon Vineyard (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Cowhorn Vineyard & Garden
summary: Certified Biodynamic 117-acre farm and winery on the upper Applegate River, founded by Bill and Barbara Steele. In 2021 they sold it to an investor group led by Katherine "Mini" Banks.

name: Brandborg Vineyard & Winery
summary: Elkton winery created in 2002 by Terry and Sue Brandborg, who moved from San Francisco after buying a hilltop property there. Its estate site is the Ferris Wheel Vineyard, and it was Wine Press Northwest's Oregon Winery of the Year in 2015.

sources.title: Brandborg Vineyard and Winery (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Kelley Fox Wines
summary: Small Willamette Valley producer founded in 2007 by Kelley Fox and her father, Gerson Stearns; its first vintage was just over 100 cases. It bottles Pinot noir from Maresh Vineyard among other sites.

name: Day Wines
summary: Willamette Valley label owned by Brianne Day, whose first vineyard-designate Pinot noir came in 2012. It is based at Day Camp, her cooperative winemaking facility in Dundee, and buys fruit from growers around the state.

name: Walter Scott Wines
summary: Eola-Amity Hills producer of Chardonnay and Pinot noir started in 2008 by Ken Pahlow and Erica Landon. Its winery was built next to Justice Vineyard in time for the 2014 vintage.

name: Antica Terra
summary: Started in 1989 by two New Yorkers; the vineyard and label were bought in June 2005 by Scott Adelson, Michael Kramer and John Mavredakis together with winemaker Maggie Harrison. Its 11-acre estate vineyard is in the Eola-Amity Hills and the first release under Harrison was the 2006 vintage.

sources.title: Antica Terra Acquires Keeler Estate Vineyard (Wine Business)

name: Hiyu Wine Farm
summary: Farm and winery in the Hood River Valley begun in 2010, when Nate Ready and China Tresemer bought seven acres; with partner Geoff Burke they completed the purchase of Pheasant Valley Winery in 2015. Its first wine was made at Antica Terra in 2012 and the next two vintages at Analemma.

name: Minimus Wines
summary: Carlton label of one-off experimental wines made by Chad Stock since 2011, later housed under the Craft Wine Co. umbrella alongside Omero Cellars and Origin.

name: Arterberry Maresh
summary: Dundee Hills label founded in 2005 by Jim Arterberry Maresh, working with his family's Maresh Vineyard on Worden Hill Road.
address: 9325 NE Worden Hill Road Dundee, OR 97115

name: Big Table Farm
summary: Winery and working farm near Gaston started in 2006 by Brian Marcy and Clare Carver, who made 150 cases that first year. It is a member of the Yamhill-Carlton AVA.

sources.title: Raising Big Table Farm: photos from a 2012 visit (Wakawaka Wine Reviews)

address: 26851 NW Williams Canyon Rd Gaston OR 97119

name: Hope Well Wine
summary: Label founded in 2016 by Mimi Casteel, built around her own vineyard and her advocacy for regenerative farming.

sources.title: Mimi Casteel would like a conversation (DM Wineline)

name: Domaine Roy & fils
summary: Willamette Valley winery founded in 2012 by Jared Etzel and Marc-André Roy, sons of Beaux Frères partners. They sold it to Marchesi Frescobaldi in 2023.

sources.title: Straight Out of the Chute at Oregon's Rodeo Hills (Wine Spectator)
Marchesi Frescobaldi to acquire Domaine Roy & fils in US expansion (Wine Business)
Former Oregon car dealer gears up with Jachter Family Wines (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Purple Hands Winery
summary: Label launched in 2005 by Cody Wright with 250 cases, made in its early years at Ken Wright Cellars and later at ROCO. Its estate site, Latchkey Vineyard in the Dundee Hills, was planted from 2012 with partners Scott and Michele Campbell.

sources.title: Purple Hands: Cody Wright (Oregon Wine Press)

name: RR Wines
summary: Small Pinot noir and Riesling brand that Harry Peterson-Nedry founded in 2002 as Ribbon Ridge Winery, made from the family's Ridgecrest Vineyards. He and his daughter Wynne moved its production to the Carlton Winemakers Studio in fall 2018.

sources.title: Last Call: Harry Peterson-Nedry (Oregon Wine Press)
Katie Santora named head winemaker at Chehalem (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Lavinea
summary: Producer of single-vineyard Pinot noir and Chardonnay from mature Willamette Valley sites, founded in 2014 by Evening Land alumni Isabelle Meunier and Greg Ralston. Its debut 2014 wines were released in 2016.

sources.title: Ellen on Wine: Isabelle Meunier keeps Lavinea winery on global stage (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Harper Voit
summary: Drew Voit's private label of Pinot noir, Pinot blanc and Riesling, based in McMinnville. Its Old Vine Riesling comes from Maresh Vineyard.

name: Tendril Wine Cellars
summary: Willamette Valley label launched in 2008 by Tony Rynders after ten years as winemaker at Domaine Serene, alongside his consulting business.

name: Analemma Wines
summary: Columbia River Gorge winery of Steven Thompson and Kris Fade, whose first releases were from 2010. It began with the leased Atavus Vineyard above White Salmon, Washington, and from 2012 planted its own land near Mosier.

sources.title: Steven Thompson and Kris Fade, young growers from Mosier, Oregon (Good Fruit Grower)

name: Ovum Wines
summary: Riesling-focused label founded in 2011 by John House and Ksenija Kostic, sourcing fruit from vineyards across Oregon.

name: Matzinger Davies Wine Co
summary: Family label of winemakers Anna Matzinger and Michael Davies, producing Eola-Amity Hills Pinot noir, Chardonnay and Columbia Gorge Sauvignon blanc. Prince of Pinot records the wines as made at the Rex Hill facility.

sources.title: Matzinger Davies Wine Co (Prince of Pinot)

name: Haden Fig
summary: Erin Nuccio's own label, first made in 2007 at Evesham Wood with Russ Raney's help and now run alongside it.

sources.title: Erin Nuccio, Evesham Wood | Haden Fig (Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers)

name: Valley View Vineyard (Peter Britt)
summary: Peter Britt's nineteenth-century vineyard and winery at Jacksonville, described as Oregon's first winery. It stopped production when Britt died in 1905; the Wisnovsky family's Valley View Winery in the Applegate Valley, planted in 1972, is a separate business named in its honor.

sources.title: Vineyards of the Rogue Valley (Rogue Valley Winegrowers Association)
As It Was: Peter Britt Becomes Early Oregon Winemaker (Jefferson Public Radio)

name: Doerner Winery
summary: The Doerner family's winery on Heydon Road near Roseburg, bonded as Oregon winery No. 7 and described as the Umpqua Valley's first post-Prohibition winery. Accounts of its dates differ: bonded by 1923 or opened in 1934, building erected 1935, closed by 1953 or run by Adolph's son until 1965. Richard Sommer bought its equipment for HillCrest Vineyard.

sources.title: Way-Back Wine: Doerner Vineyards (Oregon Wine Press)
Umpqua Valley Wine History (Umpqua Valley Winegrowers Association)

name: Honeywood Winery
summary: Salem fruit and grape winery founded by Ron Honeyman and John Wood as Columbia Distilleries, bonded on 6 December 1933 and incorporated in December 1934; it took the Honeywood name by 1937. It is described as the oldest continuously operating winery in Oregon.

sources.title: Way-Back Wine: Doerner Vineyards (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Well Played Wines
summary: Newberg label founded by Megan Markel that makes low-alcohol sparkling wines of around 7 to 7.5% ABV.

name: Granville Wine Co.
summary: Dundee Hills producer of Pinot noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wine run by second-generation grower Jackson Holstein and his wife Ayla.

name: Lytle-Barnett
summary: Vintage-dated traditional-method sparkling wine label founded by Andy Lytle, estate-grown in the Eola-Amity Hills.

name: Aubaine
summary: Single-vineyard Chardonnay and Pinot noir label founded by Andy Lytle, grown at Anahata Vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills with Isabelle Meunier as winemaker.

name: Beckham Estate Vineyard
summary: Chehalem Mountains estate near Sherwood founded by Andrew and Annedria Beckham, who began planting in 2005 and made their first wines in 2009. Andrew, a ceramicist, makes the terracotta amphorae in which the wines are fermented and aged.

name: Corollary Wines
summary: Sparkling-only Willamette Valley producer founded in 2017 by Jeanne Feldkamp and Dan Diephouse, who bought land in the Eola-Amity Hills in 2022 and began planting an estate vineyard in 2023.

sources.title: Corollary Wines' new sparkling wine tasting room (Portland Monthly)
Weinnotes podcast: Dan and Jeanne, Corollary Wines (YouTube)

name: CHO Wines
summary: Winery founded in 2021 by married couple Dave and Lois Cho, reported as Oregon's first Korean American winemakers; they bought a property in the Chehalem Mountains the following year.

sources.title: Championing AAPI Representation in Wine (SevenFifty Daily)
Weinnotes podcast: Dave and Lois Cho, CHO Wines (YouTube)

name: Rodeo Hills
summary: Dundee Hills label from Jared Etzel and Eugene Labunsky, based on a small field-blend vineyard on Worden Hill Road that was planted on a former pear farm with cuttings selected from Beaux Freres.
address: 10275 NE Worden Hill Rd Dundee, OR 97115

name: Marchesi Frescobaldi
summary: Tuscan wine family firm with some 700 years of winemaking history, which bought Oregon's Domaine Roy & fils in 2023.

sources.title: Marchesi Frescobaldi to acquire Domaine Roy & fils in US expansion (Wine Business)

name: Lenné Estate
summary: Willamette Valley vineyard estate and brand run for 22 years by Steve Lutz, who sold the estate in late 2022, and then the brand, to Jory, LLC, a venture of Eugene Labunsky and Jared Etzel.

name: Jachter Family Wines
summary: Family winery in the Chehalem Mountains near Newberg started by former car dealer Dave Jachter and his wife Karen; its first wines were from 2019, made by Jared Etzel from purchased fruit while the estate vineyard was established. The tasting room opened in 2023.

sources.title: Former Oregon car dealer gears up with Jachter Family Wines (Great Northwest Wine)

name: 00 Wines
summary: Willamette Valley producer for which Wynne Peterson-Nedry was formerly winemaker, earning high critical scores.

name: Arlyn
summary: Small Willamette Valley label whose wines are made by Wynne Peterson-Nedry.

name: Celestial Hill
summary: Small Willamette Valley producer for which Wynne Peterson-Nedry consults.

name: Compris Vineyard
summary: Newberg estate formerly known as Vidon Vineyard, renamed under proprietors Dru and Erin Allen; Aaron Kendall became winemaker in 2023.

name: Greywing Wines
summary: Label of Ari and Brandy Grey, a featured winery at the 2023 IPNC. Its estate vineyard is named Blackfeather after Brandy's Shawnee ancestor Johnson Blackfeather.

sources.title: Weinnotes podcast: Rooted in Legacy: A Journey with Greywing Wines (YouTube)

name: Open Claim Vineyards
summary: Estate outside Dallas, Oregon, owned by Brett and Marnie Wall on land Marnie's mother bought in 1994, with Chardonnay and Pinot noir planted in 2012. Tony Rynders makes the wines; the first public release was the 2015 vintage.

name: Keeler Estate Vineyard
summary: Willamette Valley estate acquired by Antica Terra in 2023; Nicholas Keeler was its winemaker.

sources.title: Antica Terra Acquires Keeler Estate Vineyard (Wine Business)

name: Authentique
summary: Willamette Valley label made by winemaker Nicholas Keeler.

name: Chosen Family Wines
summary: Willamette Valley wine brand started in 2020 by former NBA player Channing Frye with Kevin Love, Chase Renton and Jacob Gray; it releases collaborations with Oregon wineries.

sources.title: Weinnotes podcast: Channing Frye, Chosen Family Wines (YouTube)

name: Lonesome Rock
summary: Estate label of Danny and Susan Klieman from their vineyard in the Coast Range foothills west of Carlton; Isabelle Dutartre makes the Pinot noir and Jackson Holstein the Chardonnay.

name: De Ponte Cellars
summary: Dundee Hills winery started in 2001 by Scott and Rae Baldwin, with Isabelle Dutartre as winemaker since that year.

name: 1789 Wines
summary: Isabelle Dutartre's own label, founded after she settled permanently in Oregon in the mid-2000s.

name: Ambar
summary: Willamette Valley estate owned by Rob Townsend, described as the valley's first Regenerative Organic Certified vineyard, with wines made by Kate Payne Brown.
address: 12550 NE Worden Hill Rd Newberg, OR 97132

name: Human Cellars
summary: Small Willamette Valley label of winemaker Bryan Berenguer, who took part in the 2023 Indie Wine Mixer.

name: Arabilis
summary: Small Willamette Valley producer of sparkling and still wines made by Kenny McMahon and run with his wife.

name: Audeant
summary: Small Willamette Valley Pinot noir and Chardonnay producer whose bottlings include a Seven Springs Vineyard Chardonnay.

name: Morgen Long
summary: Willamette Valley label of Seth Morgen Long, devoted solely to Chardonnay.

name: Domaine Divio
summary: Newberg winery of Burgundy-born winemaker Bruno Corneaux and his wife Isabelle.

sources.title: Weinnotes podcast: Bruno Corneaux, Domaine Divio (YouTube)

address: 16435 NE Lewis Rogers Lane, Newberg, OR 97132

name: Walnut Ridge Vineyard
summary: Estate winery west of Junction City in the Lower Long Tom AVA, owned by Aaron and Alisha Young, with vines dating from 1996 and Andrew Smith as winemaker.

name: Antiquum Farm
summary: Junction City estate known for the grazing-based viticulture practised by Stephen Hagen.

name: Approachment
summary: Small Willamette Valley label started by the married winemakers Jess and Paden West, known for Chardonnay, Gamay and traditional-method sparkling; it operates out of Benza Vineyard.

sources.title: Weinnotes podcast: Paden and Jess West of Approachment (YouTube)

name: Benza Vineyard
summary: Willamette Valley winery where Paden West has been head winemaker since 2022; Approachment also makes its wines there.

name: LucidWild Estate
summary: Dundee Hills estate opened to visitors in 2025 by Blair and L.J. Nicholas on the former Bella Vida Vineyard property on Worden Hill Road, with Isabelle Meunier directing the winemaking.

sources.title: Blair & L.J. Nicholas interview (Oregon Wine History Archive)
Weinnotes podcast: Blair and LJ of LucidWild (YouTube)

name: Red Electric
summary: Ribbon Ridge label of retired physician Doug Ackerman, named for an early electric rail line out of Portland; all fruit comes from the family's Armstrong Vineyard and John Grochau has made the wines since 2015.

name: Grochau Cellars
summary: John Grochau's own label, founded in 2002, with a tasting room in Portland.

name: EIEIO & Company
summary: One-person Willamette Valley winery owned and run by winemaker Jay McDonald, making small lots of Pinot noir and Chardonnay from purchased fruit.

name: Ghost Hill Cellars
summary: Yamhill-Carlton winery on a farm the Bayliss family has held since 1906. The family planted vines in 1999 to sell grapes and started the label in 2006 after a buyer paid for fruit with unlabeled wine.

name: Le Cadeau Vineyard
summary: Pinot noir estate of Tom and Deb Mortimer on Parrett Mountain, with a tasting room in Dundee. The owners have engaged a succession of outside winemakers and consultants for wines from their multi-clone vineyard.

name: Late Sky
summary: Dundee Hills estate on Herring Lane near Newberg, a partnership between winemaker Jared Etzel and Glenn and Karen Fischer. Etzel bought the land in 2015, the partners began the project in 2016, and the winery and tasting room opened in 2024.

name: Coattails
summary: Willamette Valley wine label listed in 2024 among the projects Jared Etzel makes wine for.

name: Tekstura
summary: Willamette Valley wine label listed in 2024 among the projects Jared Etzel makes wine for.

name: Sequitur
summary: Willamette Valley wine label listed in 2024 among the projects Jared Etzel makes wine for.

name: Alexana Winery
summary: Willamette Valley winery where Bryan Weil was winemaker before joining Vinovate.

name: Joseph Phelps Vineyards
summary: Napa Valley estate known for the Insignia red blend, where Craig Williams was winemaker for more than three decades.

name: Abbott Claim
summary: Willamette Valley winery whose wines, including an X Omni Vineyard Chardonnay, are made by Alban Debeaulieu.

name: Violin
summary: Small Willamette Valley producer whose wines include an X Omni Vineyard Pinot noir.

name: Johan Vineyards
summary: Van Duzer Corridor estate bought in October 2021 by the same ownership group as Cowhorn, which calls it a sister property.

name: Apona Vineyards
summary: New estate winery in Veneta, in the southern Willamette Valley west of Eugene, founded by Andrew Head and Afton Towry; its young vineyard includes Sauvignon blanc, Sangiovese, Lagrein and five Pinot noir clones.

name: Wente Vineyards
summary: California winery where Chris Graves interned and then worked full time before moving to Oregon.

name: Arborbrook
summary: Biodynamically farmed winery on Calkins Lane, next door to Adelsheim, under the same ownership as Cooper Mountain Vineyards.

name: Cooper Mountain Vineyards
summary: Biodynamic Willamette Valley winery whose owners also own Arborbrook.

name: Dusky Goose
summary: Willamette Valley winery whose winemaker Hans left the post around the start of 2026.

name: Anne Amie Vineyards
summary: Willamette Valley winery formerly known as Chateau Benoit.

name: Dominio IV
summary: Oregon winery, with Patrick Reuter as winemaker, that makes both Pinot noir and bigger red varieties.

name: Maison Jussiaume
summary: Jean-Michel Jussiaume's Oregon sparkling-only house, which hand riddles and disgorges its wines.

name: Iterum Wines
summary: Joe Dobbes's small Salem-based label, making still and sparkling wine.

name: Sun Break Wines
summary: Oregon producer, with David Patte as winemaker, that pours at Eola-Amity Hills events.

name: Ricochet
summary: Erich Berg's Oregon wine label, which opened a winery to visitors in September 2024.

name: Dukes Family Vineyards
summary: Small estate winery near Amity owned by Pat and Jackie Dukes, producing Pinot noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wine.

name: Mad Violets Wine Co.
summary: Boutique Willamette Valley label of winemaker Kelly Kidneigh and vineyard manager Stirling Fox.

name: Doubleback
summary: Walla Walla Cabernet producer started in 2007 by Drew Bledsoe with Chris Figgins as founding winemaker; flagship of Bledsoe Wine Estates.

name: Bledsoe McDaniels
summary: Label of Drew Bledsoe and winemaker Josh McDaniels for single-vineyard Walla Walla Syrah and Willamette Valley Pinot noir. In 2021 the group bought Mimi Casteel's Hope Well vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills.

name: Weisinger Family Winery
summary: Ashland winery in the Bear Creek Valley of the Rogue Valley, opened by John Weisinger in 1988 as Weisinger's of Ashland beside Gewurztraminer vines planted in 1978. Now run by his son Eric, with a large custom-crush business.

name: R. Stuart & Co. Winery
summary: McMinnville winery founded in 2001 by winemaker Rob Stuart and his wife Maria, with a tasting room on Third Street.

name: David Paige Wines
summary: Label started by former Adelsheim winemaker David Paige after he left that winery in 2017.

name: McCollum Heritage 91
summary: Wine label of CJ and Elise McCollum, first made in partnership with Adelsheim in 2019; the family has since developed its own McCollum Family Vineyard in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA.

name: de Lancellotti Family Vineyards
summary: Biodynamically farmed family estate on Calkins Lane near Newberg. The vineyard was planted in 2001 and the brand created in 2005; wines are made with Robert Brittan.

name: Brittan Vineyards
summary: Estate of Robert and Ellen Brittan on a 128-acre property at the western edge of the Willamette Valley bought in 2004, growing Pinot noir, Chardonnay and Rhone varieties.

name: Et Fille Wines
summary: Newberg winery founded in 2003 by Howard Mozeico and his daughter Jessica, who now runs it and makes the wines, including vineyard-designated Pinot noirs and a sparkling wine.

name: Lundeen Wines
summary: McMinnville label of Michael Lundeen, under his own name since 2008, making Pinot noir, Chardonnay and traditional-method sparkling wine sold largely through distribution.

name: Privé Vineyard
summary: Small estate winery off Bell Road near Newberg, bought in 2020 by Piper Underbrink, who has since added a second estate vineyard.

name: Amaterra
summary: Large winery, restaurant and members' venue on Swede Hill in Portland's West Hills, opened in late 2021 by the founders of the Touchmark retirement-community company.
address: 8150 SW Swede Hill Drive Portland, OR 97225

name: 51Weeks
summary: Wine label started by Matt Vuylsteke, now poured alongside the Amaterra wines.

name: Hazelfern Cellars
summary: Family winery of Bryan and Laura Laing, begun in a Portland basement and now based in a converted barn near Newberg.

name: Vincent Wine Company
summary: One-person Willamette Valley label of Vincent Fritzsche, sold mostly through spring and autumn mailing-list releases.

name: White Walnut Estate
summary: Dundee Hills estate on Trunk Road that Chris Mazepink carved out of an abandoned 11-acre walnut orchard bought in 2013, planted in 2015 and 2016 and opened to visitors in April 2021. Farmed organically and biodynamically as a polyculture.

name: Dobbes Family Estate
summary: Winery founded in 2002 by Joe Dobbes, together with the larger-volume Wine by Joe brand, after he left Willamette Valley Vineyards.

sources.title: Joe Dobbes: Third Decade's a Charm (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Atticus Wine
summary: Small Willamette Valley producer owned by winemaker Ximena Orrego.

name: Laura Volkman Vineyards
summary: Small Chehalem Mountains producer with a mailing-list following, built around the 3.5-acre Elle Reve vineyard planted about 2002. Illness forced Laura Volkman to sell in 2012, and the property became Potter's Vineyard.

name: Potter's Vineyard
summary: Winery and pottery gallery near Newberg run by Bill and Sandy Sanchez, who bought the former Laura Volkman property in 2012 and bottle under the Vino Vasai label. Named Oregon's Winery to Watch for 2022 by Great Northwest Wine.

name: Dion Vineyard
summary: Family vineyard and winery near Cornelius on land Ron and Joanne Johnson bought in 1973, now about 60 acres. The family sold its grapes until its first commercial wine in the mid-2000s; Kevin Johnson and Beth Klingner make Pinot noir, Pinot gris and sparkling wine.

name: Siltstone Wines
summary: Myers family winery near Dayton, established in 2000, known for selling older vintages at modest prices from a tasting room beside Highway 18.

name: L'Angolo Estate
summary: Willamette Valley estate winery for which Isabelle Meunier is consulting winemaker.

name: Leah Jørgensen Cellars
summary: Oregon label established in 2011 that centres on Cabernet franc from Southern Oregon vineyards.

name: Trisaetum
summary: Ribbon Ridge winery making Pinot noir, Chardonnay and Riesling, with sparkling wine under the Pashey label. In 2022 the family added Brixeur Spirits, a distillery and tasting bar on the estate.

name: Irvine & Roberts Vineyards
summary: Southern Oregon winery where Vince Vidrine worked before joining Cowhorn.

name: White Rose Estate
summary: Small Willamette Valley winery where Tresider Burns led winemaking for three vintages before moving to Alexana in 2022.

sources.title: Tresider Burns named winemaker for Alexana Winery (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Leonetti Cellar
summary: Walla Walla winery where Chris Figgins makes the wine and Josh McDaniels trained.

name: Toil Oregon
summary: Chris Figgins's Oregon Pinot noir project, on which Josh McDaniels also worked.

name: Methven Family Vineyards
summary: Eola-Amity Hills estate of 85 acres, 30 of them planted, with a winery and tasting room; bought by Domaine Drouhin Oregon in 2022.

sources.title: Domaine Drouhin Oregon acquires Methven Family Vineyards (Wine Business)

name: Bells Up Winery
summary: Small Newberg winery on Bell Road founded in 2013 by Dave and Sara Specter. It hosts one group at a time and grows Seyval blanc alongside Pinot noir.

name: de la boue
summary: Small Willamette Valley label started by Travis Todd and Chris Andrew, with a first vintage in 2019. It makes single-vineyard Chardonnay, Pinot noir and Syrah.

name: Wine by Joe
summary: Value-priced Oregon wine brand that Joe Dobbes started in 2002 alongside Dobbes Family Estate.

sources.title: Joe Dobbes: Third decade's a charm (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Integrated Beverage Group
summary: Oregon wine company whose brands include Rascal and Duck Pond; Travis Todd became its head winemaker in 2020.

name: Domaine Willamette
summary: Sparkling wine house and visitor centre built by Willamette Valley Vineyards off Highway 99 near Dundee; it opened to shareholders over Labor Day weekend 2022.

name: J. Christopher Wines
summary: Newberg winery started by Jay Somers; the Appassionata Estate project operates under its roof.

name: Left Coast Estate
summary: 500-acre family-run estate at Rickreall with roughly 150 to 160 acres of vines, founded in 2003 with a first vintage in 2004. Known for white Pinot noir and for its oak savanna conservation work.
address: 4225 North Pacific Hwy W, Rickreall, OR, 97371

name: Belle Vallée Cellars
summary: Oregon winery and custom-crush operation that Joe Wright joined in 2002 with Steve Allen and Mike Magee.

name: J. Wright Vintner
summary: Joe Wright's own label, made with support from Left Coast Estate from Left Coast, Chehalem Mountains and Eola-Amity Hills fruit.

name: Pfeiffer Winery
summary: Junction City winery and 70-acre vineyard of Robin and Danuta Pfeiffer, dating to 1983; King Estate bought it in November 2022.

sources.title: King Estate acquires Pfeiffer Winery (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Owen Roe
summary: Northwest winery formerly owned by David O'Reilly.

name: Distaff Wine
summary: Newberg wine label created by Angelica O'Reilly and her daughters.

name: Andante Vineyard
summary: Van Duzer Corridor estate near Dallas, Oregon, with a new tasting room beside a wildlife refuge; it grows Aligoté alongside Pinot noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon blanc.

name: Niew Vineyards
summary: Small allocation-only Willamette Valley label whose wine is made by Seth Morgen Long.

name: Call Me Dolores
summary: Kate Payne Brown's own label, making Pinot noir and a sparkling Pinot blanc.

name: J.L. Kiff Vineyard
summary: Husband-and-wife estate outside McMinnville run by Joel and Laurie Kiff, who began planting in 2005 and made their first wine in 2010.

name: Cramoisi Vineyard
summary: Small family estate on Worden Hill Road in the Dundee Hills, planted from 2012 and run by a husband-and-wife team. Drew Voit was making its wines in 2020-21.
address: 8670 NE Worden Hill Rd, Dundee, OR 97115

name: Elizabeth Chambers Cellar
summary: McMinnville winery whose wines Drew Voit was making in 2020-21, including single-vineyard Pinot noirs from Temperance Hill, Lazy River and Dupee.

name: Van Duzer Vineyards
summary: Estate established in 1998 by Carl and Marilynn Thoma near Dallas, Oregon, in what is now the Van Duzer Corridor AVA, with 83 acres of vines there and a second 38-acre site off Worden Hill Road in Dundee.

name: Utopia Vineyard
summary: Ribbon Ridge estate of Dan Warnshuis, who bought 19 acres in 2000, planted in 2002 and made his first vintage in 2005.

name: Angela Vineyards
summary: Antony Beck's Oregon Pinot noir label, begun on the lower part of the Abbott Claim property that he bought from Ken Wright in 2006. Alban Debeaulieu became its winemaker in 2017.

name: Alloro Vineyard
summary: Estate on Laurelwood soils in the Chehalem Mountains near Sherwood. David Nemarnik began planting in 1999, the first vintage was 2002 and Tom Fitzpatrick has made the wine since 2010.

name: Élevée Winegrowers
summary: Tom Fitzpatrick's own label, based in Dundee, with a terroir-focused range that includes a Riesling from Ridgecrest Vineyards.

name: King's North
summary: Family-run Newberg winery started by brothers Sid and Mac Heinze, with five acres of estate Pinot noir planted in 2018 and purchased fruit that includes Luminous Hills Pinot noir.

name: Youngberg Hill
summary: Hilltop inn, vineyard and winery outside McMinnville. Norman Barnett bought the land in 1987 to build the inn, the first vines went in in 1989, and Wayne Bailey bought the property in 2003 and moved it to organic, then biodynamic, farming.
address: 10660 SW Youngberg Hill Road McMinnville, OR 97128

name: Bryn Mawr Vineyards
summary: Eola-Amity Hills estate across the road from Temperance Hill, bought by Jon and Kathy Lauer in 2009 and built up by winemaker and vineyard manager Rachel Rose to 32 acres of vines. A winery was added in 2018 and a tasting room in 2019.

name: Rain Dance Vineyards
summary: Newberg estate label of Ken Austin, who at first only sold grapes and started the brand after buyers dropped contracts in the wet 2013 harvest, at the suggestion of Bryan Weil, who makes the wine.

name: Hummingbird Estate
summary: Winery and bed and breakfast in a 1926 house at Central Point, opened to the public in 2019 by Illinois farmers Ed and Susan Walk.

name: RoxyAnn Winery
summary: Medford winery on the historic Hillcrest Orchard estate, where Jack Day planted the first 20 acres of vines in 1997; its first wine was a 2001 Claret.

name: Belle Fiore Winery
summary: Ashland estate winery whose wines have been made by Rob Folin.

name: Winter's Hill Estate
summary: Family winery in the Dundee Hills on a farm bought by John and Lena Winter in 1961. Their daughter Emily Gladhart and her husband Peter planted its vineyard, and their son Russell is the winemaker.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Month feature: Winter's Hill Estate (1000 Friends of Oregon)
Bees, Birds and Pinot Take Center Stage at Winter's Hill Estate (Portland Monthly, sponsored)

name: Guillén Family Wines
summary: Pinot noir label created by Jesús Guillén alongside his work at White Rose Estate, begun with fruit from Vista Hills Vineyard. Sources date the start to a first wine in 2006 or a launch in 2009 with the 2007 vintage.

sources.title: Guillén Family Wines (The Prince of Pinot)
Jesús Guillén Olvera (1980–2018): Réquiem para un gentilhombre (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Fox Farm Vineyards
summary: Small family-owned label making Pinot noir and other wines from leased parcels in several Willamette Valley sub-AVAs and Syrah from the Rogue Valley, with Joe Dobbes as winemaker. Its first Pinot noir was the 2006 vintage. Despite the name, it farms no named estate vineyard of its own.

sources.title: David Fish of Fox Farm Vineyards (Fox Farm Vineyards)
Fox Farm Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
